cohort: 108 neonates born via elective cesarean delivery and their fathers were recruited into this study and randomly divided into treatment and control groups.
finding: Paternal skin-to-skin contact after cesarean delivery was beneficial for newborns by stabilizing their physical conditions and increasing breastfeeding rates, and for fathers by significantly reducing anxiety and depression while facilitating their role attainment.
mod_finding: The study found that paternal skin-to-skin contact specifically after cesarean delivery was beneficial for both newborns and fathers.
